_about: Themes traced through Scripture with the Church’s reading of each. Written for this app as study aids. CCC numbers point to the Catechism sections that treat the theme; they are pointers, not quotations.

themes.title: Creation and new creation
themes.summary: From “in the beginning” to “I make all things new,” Scripture frames salvation as God’s creative work, restored and completed in Christ.

stages.label: In the beginning
stages.note: God creates by his word; creation is good and ordered toward the Sabbath.

stages.label: Humanity in God’s image
stages.note: Man and woman are made in God’s image and given care of the world.

stages.label: Wisdom at creation
stages.note: Wisdom is present at creation, a theme the New Testament applies to Christ.

stages.label: Creation praises
stages.note: The heavens and the earth declare God’s glory.

stages.label: A new creation promised
stages.note: God promises new heavens and a new earth.

stages.label: Through the Word
stages.note: All things were made through the Word and are reconciled in him.

stages.label: A new creation in Christ
stages.note: Believers are a new creation; creation itself groans for redemption.

stages.label: All things new
stages.note: The story ends with a new heaven and a new earth.

themes.catholic: The Church reads creation as the first act of God’s plan of salvation: everything is made through the Word and for Christ, and the Resurrection begins the new creation. Genesis is read for its religious truth (who made the world and why), not as a scientific account.

themes.title: Covenant
themes.summary: God binds himself to his people by oath and love, from Noah to the new covenant in Christ’s blood.

stages.label: Noah
stages.note: God makes an everlasting covenant with all creatures; the rainbow is its sign.

stages.label: Abraham
stages.note: Land, descendants and blessing for all nations; circumcision as sign.

stages.label: Sinai
stages.note: Israel is called a priestly kingdom; the covenant is sealed with blood.

stages.label: David
stages.note: An everlasting house and throne for David’s line.

stages.label: Broken and renewed
stages.note: Israel breaks the covenant; the prophets call it back.

stages.label: A new covenant promised
stages.note: The law will be written on hearts; God will give a new spirit.

stages.label: Sealed in Christ’s blood
stages.note: At the Last Supper Jesus gives the cup of the new covenant.

stages.label: Wedding of the Lamb
stages.note: The covenant is fulfilled in God dwelling with his people.

themes.catholic: The Church sees one plan of salvation unfolding in successive covenants, each preparing for the new and eternal covenant in Christ, which the Eucharist makes present.

themes.title: Exodus and Passover
themes.summary: God’s liberation of Israel from slavery becomes the pattern for all later deliverance, culminating in Christ’s Passover.

stages.label: Slavery and call
stages.note: God hears the cry of his people and reveals his name to Moses.

stages.label: Passover
stages.note: The lamb’s blood on the doorposts; a memorial feast.

stages.label: Through the sea
stages.note: God saves his people through the water.

stages.label: Manna in the wilderness
stages.note: Bread from heaven and daily dependence on God.

stages.label: A second exodus
stages.note: The prophets promise a new exodus from exile.

stages.label: Christ’s Passover
stages.note: Jesus is the Lamb of God; the Last Supper is a Passover meal.

stages.label: Baptism and exodus
stages.note: Paul reads the sea and the cloud as figures of baptism.

stages.label: The song of the Lamb
stages.note: The redeemed sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb.

themes.catholic: The Fathers read the Passover and the crossing of the sea as types of Christ’s death and resurrection and of baptism; the Eucharist is the new Passover.

themes.title: Temple and the presence of God
themes.summary: From the tabernacle to Christ’s body to the Church, God chooses to dwell with his people.

stages.label: Garden as sanctuary
stages.note: Eden is where God walks with humanity.

stages.label: The tabernacle
stages.note: God’s glory fills the tent.

stages.label: Solomon’s Temple
stages.note: The glory fills the Temple; God cannot be contained.

stages.label: Prophets and the Temple
stages.note: The glory departs and is promised to return.

stages.label: The Word tabernacled
stages.note: The Word “pitched his tent” among us; Jesus’ body is the new Temple.

stages.label: The Church as Temple
stages.note: Believers are living stones in God’s house.

stages.label: The Temple is the Lord
stages.note: In the new Jerusalem the Lord God and the Lamb are its temple.

themes.catholic: The Church sees the Temple fulfilled in Christ’s body and in the Church; the liturgy is a participation in the heavenly worship.

themes.title: Kingdom and Messiah
themes.summary: God’s kingship, promised through David, comes near in Jesus the Messiah.

stages.label: God is King
stages.note: Israel confesses the Lord as king.

stages.label: Israel asks for a king
stages.note: The monarchy begins; God’s choice looks at the heart.

stages.label: The Davidic promise
stages.note: An anointed king and son of God whose throne will last.

stages.label: Prophecy of a coming king
stages.note: A child, a shoot of Jesse, a ruler from Bethlehem.

stages.label: The Son of Man
stages.note: One like a son of man receives an everlasting kingdom.

stages.label: The kingdom has come near
stages.note: Jesus proclaims the kingdom in word and deed.

stages.label: The King crucified and risen
stages.note: Jesus’ kingship is revealed on the cross and in the Resurrection.

stages.label: The reign completed
stages.note: The kingdom of the world becomes the kingdom of our Lord.

themes.catholic: The Church receives Christ as the Messiah, the Son of David, and proclaims that the kingdom is already present in him and in the Church while awaiting its fulfilment.

themes.title: The shepherd and the flock
themes.summary: Israel’s kings and God himself are shepherds; Jesus is the Good Shepherd who lays down his life.

stages.label: The Lord is my shepherd
stages.note: God leads and protects his flock.

stages.label: Moses and David as shepherds
stages.note: God raises shepherds for his people.

stages.label: Bad shepherds
stages.note: God condemns shepherds who feed themselves and promises to shepherd the flock himself.

stages.label: A shepherd in David’s line
stages.note: A servant like David will shepherd Israel.

stages.label: The Good Shepherd
stages.note: Jesus knows his sheep and gives his life for them.

stages.label: Feed my sheep
stages.note: Peter and the elders are charged to tend the flock.

stages.label: The Lamb as shepherd
stages.note: The Lamb will shepherd the redeemed.

themes.catholic: The Church’s pastors share in Christ’s own shepherding; the Church is the sheepfold whose gate is Christ.

themes.title: Sacrifice and priesthood
themes.summary: From Abel’s offering to the one sacrifice of Christ, the Bible shows how God’s people draw near to him.

stages.label: Abel and Noah
stages.note: The earliest offerings.

stages.label: Melchizedek
stages.note: A priest-king offers bread and wine.

stages.label: The binding of Isaac
stages.note: The beloved son and the provided lamb.

stages.label: The Levitical system
stages.note: Offerings, priests and the Day of Atonement.

stages.label: Mercy over sacrifice
stages.note: The prophets insist sacrifice must flow from a faithful heart.

stages.label: The Servant gives himself
stages.note: One who bears the sins of many.

stages.label: The one sacrifice
stages.note: Christ the high priest offers himself once for all.

stages.label: The sacrifice of praise and the Mass
stages.note: A pure offering among all nations; believers offer themselves; the Lamb is worshiped.

themes.catholic: The Church holds that Christ’s one sacrifice on the cross is made present in the Eucharist, and that the ministerial priesthood serves the priesthood of all the baptised.

themes.title: Sabbath and rest
themes.summary: God’s rest at creation becomes the pattern of worship and the promise of a final rest.

stages.label: God rests
stages.note: The seventh day is blessed and made holy.

stages.label: Sabbath in the law
stages.note: Rest remembers creation and liberation.

stages.label: Sabbath year and jubilee
stages.note: A rhythm of release and restoration.

stages.label: Jesus and the Sabbath
stages.note: “The Sabbath was made for man”; the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.

stages.label: The first day of the week
stages.note: The Resurrection gives Christians the Lord’s Day.

stages.label: A rest that remains
stages.note: A Sabbath rest still awaits the people of God.

themes.catholic: Christians keep the Lord’s Day as the day of the Resurrection, in which creation’s rest is fulfilled and the eternal rest is foretasted.

themes.title: Marriage and the bridegroom
themes.summary: The covenant between God and his people is told in the language of marriage.

stages.label: Marriage at creation
stages.note: Two become one flesh.

stages.label: Israel as bride
stages.note: God courts, forgives and restores his unfaithful bride.

stages.label: The love song
stages.refs: Song of Songs 2:8-17; Song of Songs 8:6-7
stages.note: Read as an image of divine love.

stages.label: The bridegroom has come
stages.note: Jesus is the bridegroom.

stages.label: Marriage in Christ
stages.note: Christian marriage reflects Christ’s love for the Church.

stages.label: The wedding supper
stages.note: The marriage of the Lamb and the new Jerusalem.

themes.catholic: The Church honours marriage as a sacrament that signifies Christ’s union with the Church, and reads the Song of Songs as an image of God’s love for his people.

themes.title: Water and baptism
themes.summary: Water brings judgment and new life, from the flood to the font.

stages.label: The Spirit over the waters
stages.note: The waters of creation.

stages.label: The flood
stages.note: Judgment and a new beginning; Peter reads it as a figure of baptism.

stages.label: The Red Sea and the Jordan
stages.note: God’s people pass through the water.

stages.label: Washing and cleansing
stages.note: Water as sign of cleansing and a new spirit.

stages.label: Jesus baptised
stages.note: The Spirit descends and the Father speaks.

stages.label: Born of water and the Spirit
stages.note: New birth in baptism.

stages.label: The river of life
stages.note: Water flows from the Temple and the throne.

themes.catholic: The Church teaches that the waters of creation, the flood and the Red Sea prefigure baptism, in which the Spirit gives new birth.

themes.title: Wisdom and the Word
themes.summary: Wisdom personified in the Old Testament becomes the key to the New Testament’s description of Christ.

stages.label: The fear of the Lord
stages.note: The beginning of wisdom.

stages.label: Wisdom speaks
stages.note: Wisdom calls and dwells among God’s people.

stages.label: Wisdom and the Law
stages.note: Wisdom is identified with the book of the Law.

stages.label: Wisdom, a breath of God’s power
stages.note: A reflection of eternal light.

stages.label: The Word became flesh
stages.note: Wisdom and Word meet in the Incarnation.

stages.label: Christ the wisdom of God
stages.note: In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom.

themes.catholic: The Church reads the wisdom texts as pointing to the eternal Word, and honours the Wisdom books as inspired Scripture.

themes.title: Exile and return
themes.summary: Loss, judgment and homecoming give Israel’s prophets their message of hope.

stages.label: Expelled from Eden
stages.note: The first exile.

stages.label: Warnings
stages.note: Covenant curses and the threat of exile.

stages.label: The fall of Jerusalem
stages.note: The Temple is destroyed and the people deported.

stages.label: Songs in a strange land
stages.note: Grief and the vision of dry bones coming to life.

stages.label: Return
stages.note: Cyrus’ decree and the rebuilding.

stages.label: Exile in the Gospels
stages.note: The genealogy marks the exile; many still awaited redemption.

stages.label: Strangers and pilgrims
stages.note: Christians as exiles on the way to the heavenly homeland.

themes.catholic: The Church reads the return from exile as a figure of redemption in Christ and of the pilgrim Church on earth.

themes.title: Mercy and forgiveness
themes.summary: God’s self-revelation as “merciful and gracious” runs through Scripture, and Jesus embodies it.

stages.label: The name of the Lord
stages.note: “Merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love.”

stages.label: David’s repentance
stages.note: A king confesses and is forgiven.

stages.label: Mercy to Nineveh
stages.note: God’s mercy extends to the nations.

stages.label: The heart of God
stages.note: God’s compassion overcomes his anger.

stages.label: The Father’s embrace
stages.note: The prodigal son and Zacchaeus.

stages.label: Forgiveness given to the Church
stages.note: The risen Lord entrusts forgiveness to the apostles; forgive as you are forgiven.

stages.label: Mercy triumphs
stages.note: Rich in mercy.

themes.catholic: The Church proclaims God’s mercy as the heart of the gospel and exercises Christ’s forgiveness in the sacrament of Penance.

themes.title: The Holy Spirit
themes.summary: From the Spirit hovering over the waters to Pentecost, the Spirit gives life, speaks through the prophets and is poured out on the Church.

stages.label: Creation
stages.note: The breath of God gives life.

stages.label: Judges, kings and prophets
stages.note: The Spirit empowers chosen leaders.

stages.label: Promise of a new Spirit
stages.note: God will put his Spirit within his people.

stages.label: The anointed servant
stages.note: The Spirit rests on Jesus.

stages.label: The Counselor
stages.note: Jesus promises the Spirit of truth.

stages.label: Pentecost
stages.note: The Spirit is poured out on the Church.

stages.label: Life in the Spirit
stages.note: Children of God led by the Spirit; the fruits of the Spirit.

themes.catholic: The Church confesses the Holy Spirit as Lord and giver of life, who spoke through the prophets and is at work in the Church’s sacraments and Scripture.

themes.title: Manna and the bread of life
themes.summary: God’s feeding of his people in the wilderness is the Old Testament background for the Eucharist.

stages.label: The manna
stages.note: Bread from heaven each day.

stages.label: Bread of the Presence
stages.note: Twelve loaves set before God.

stages.label: Elijah fed
stages.note: Bread for the journey.

stages.label: Wisdom’s banquet
stages.note: Come, eat my bread.

stages.label: Multiplication of the loaves
stages.note: Jesus feeds the crowds.

stages.label: The bread of life
stages.note: “My flesh is true food”; the disciples’ hard saying.

stages.label: The Last Supper
stages.note: “This is my body”; “do this in memory of me.”

stages.label: Emmaus
stages.note: He was known to them in the breaking of the bread.

themes.catholic: The Church teaches that Christ is truly, really and substantially present in the Eucharist, and reads the manna as a figure of it.
